leaves.label: Lalava
leaves.defn: Decorative coconut-fibre (sennit, magimagi) lashing of Tonga, Fiji and Samoa, binding the beams of houses and the hulls of canoes in red and black geometric patterns, now also made as freestanding works.

leaves.label: Sweetgrass Baskets
leaves.defn: Coiled baskets of sweetgrass, bulrush and pine needle sewn with palmetto by the Gullah Geechee of the South Carolina Lowcountry, a West African coiling tradition: fanner baskets, sewing baskets.

leaves.label: Panier de Mayun
leaves.defn: The willow and bramble baskets of Mayun in the Brière marshes (Loire-Atlantique).

leaves.label: Bastabinne
leaves.defn: Swedish baskets plaited from strips of spruce bast.

leaves.label: Birch-Bark Crafts
leaves.defn: Containers, boxes, footwear and objects of folded, woven, sewn and carved birch bark made across Finland, Karelia and Russia: tuohikontti backpacks, tuesok boxes, woven bast shoes.

leaves.label: Shemogodsk Carving
leaves.defn: Openwork carving of birch bark from the Shemoksa river near Veliky Ustyug since the early 19th century, called 'northern lace', on boxes and tuesoks.

leaves.label: Pärekori
leaves.defn: Finnish baskets plaited from pulled wood shingles (päre).
leaves.aliases: shingle basket;making of shingle baskets from pulled shingles
rows: Making of shingle baskets from pulled shingles

leaves.label: Clubrush Work of Kruunupyy
leaves.defn: Weaving of clubrush (bulrush) into mats and objects in Kruunupyy (Kronoby), Finland.

leaves.label: Himmeli
leaves.defn: Geometric hanging mobiles of straw tubes threaded together, made at Christmas in Finland and the Baltic (Lithuanian sodai).

leaves.label: Straw Weaving in Belarus
leaves.defn: Belarusian straw weaving of ritual and decorative objects — figures, baskets, spiders (paŭki) and boxes (UNESCO 2025).
rows: Straw weaving in Belarus, art, craft and skills

leaves.label: Turiisk Straw Plaiting
leaves.defn: Straw plaiting tradition of Turiisk hromada in Volyn Oblast (Ukraine).
rows: tradition of straw plaiting in Turiisk hromada, Volyn Oblast

leaves.label: Iza Vine Weaving
leaves.defn: Willow-vine basket and furniture weaving of the village of Iza in Zakarpattia (Ukraine).

leaves.label: Shchitky Reed Weaving
leaves.defn: Reed weaving tradition of Shchitky and Pysarivka (Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine).
rows: traditions of reed weaving in Shchitky and Pysarivka

leaves.label: Wayuu Weaving
leaves.defn: the crocheted and loom-woven fibre work of Wayuu women of the Guajira Peninsula (Colombia and Venezuela), with named geometric kanaas designs: mochila (susu) bags, chinchorro hammocks.
leaves.aliases: Wayuu mochila; susu; tejido wayuu; kanaas
leaves.see: H8-2 Noken; H2-7 Andean Textiles. Possession taxonomy: Wayuu mochila (A4 Bags & Accessories).

leaves.label: Kiondo
leaves.defn: twined bags of sisal and other vegetable twine with leather trim made by Kikuyu, Kamba and Taita women of Kenya, patterned in dyed bands.
leaves.see: H8-2 Noken; H8-10 Agaseke. Possession taxonomy: Kiondo (A4 Bags & Accessories).

leaves.label: Skep
leaves.defn: coiled-straw (earlier wicker) beehives sewn with bramble strips by skeppers of northern and western Europe and the British Isles, from the Middle Ages: straw skeps, skep caps.
leaves.see: H8-30 Bastabinne. Possession taxonomy: Skep (B10 Animal Equipment); skep cap (B10 Animal Equipment); bee bole (B10 Animal Equipment).

leaves.label: Nantucket Lightship Baskets
leaves.defn: rattan-and-cane baskets woven over wooden moulds with solid turned bases, first by keepers of the Nantucket lightships in the 19th century, later lidded purses with carved ivory and scrimshaw.
leaves.see: D2-12 Scrimshaw. Possession taxonomy: Basketry cane, reed and splint (C4 Craft & Art Supplies).
rows: · owned as Basketry cane, reed and splint (Possession C4) · https://nha.org/history-online/nantucket-lightship-baskets/

leaves.label: Zulu Beadwork
leaves.defn: Glass-bead regalia of the Zulu of KwaZulu-Natal in brick stitch, with colour codes by region and age: ucu necklaces, love-letter panels (incwadi), beaded aprons and skirts.

leaves.label: Maasai Beadwork
leaves.defn: Beaded collars, earrings and headdresses of the Maasai of Kenya and Tanzania: flat disc collars, wedding necklaces.

leaves.label: Yoruba Beadwork
leaves.defn: Beaded regalia of Yoruba kings and Ifa priests: beaded crowns with veils (ade), diviners' bags, beaded staffs.

leaves.label: Mexican Featherwork
leaves.defn: Feather mosaic of Mesoamerica and colonial New Spain (amanteca), from Aztec shields and headdresses to Christian feather paintings: Moctezuma's headdress, Mass of Saint Gregory (1539).

leaves.label: Porcupine Quillwork
leaves.defn: Embroidery with flattened dyed porcupine quills on hide and birchbark across the Plains, Subarctic and Northeast: Lakota quilled robes and shirts, Mi'kmaq and Odawa quilled birchbark boxes, Dene quilled bands.

leaves.label: Plains Beadwork
leaves.defn: Glass-bead embroidery of the peoples of the Great Plains and Plateau in lane-stitch and overlay techniques, in tribal styles: Lakota fully beaded vests and cradleboards, Crow (Apsáalooke) horse gear, Blackfeet and Cree floral beadwork.
leaves.see: H9-5 Porcupine Quillwork;H9-7 Haudenosaunee Raised Beadwork

leaves.label: Haudenosaunee Raised Beadwork
leaves.defn: Raised (embossed) glass beadwork on velvet by Mohawk, Tuscarora and Seneca women, above all the 'whimsies' (pincushions, frames, purses) sold at Niagara Falls from the mid-19th century.

leaves.label: Wampum
leaves.defn: Tubular beads of white whelk and purple quahog shell strung and woven into belts and strings by the Haudenosaunee and Algonquian peoples of the Northeast to record treaties and council business: Hiawatha Belt, Two Row Wampum.

leaves.label: Hawaiian Featherwork
leaves.defn: The featherwork of the Hawaiian chiefs: red and yellow honeyeater and ʻiʻiwi feathers knotted to olonā netting as emblems of rank and divinity: ʻahu ʻula cloaks and capes, mahiole helmets, lei hulu, feathered god images.

leaves.label: Kahu Huruhuru
leaves.defn: Māori feather cloaks: muka cloaks finger-woven (whatu) with feathers of kiwi, kererū, kākā and other birds set in the weft, the highest-ranking cloaks of the 19th century onward: kahu kiwi, kahu kererū.

leaves.label: Jutti
leaves.defn: embroidered leather slip-on shoes of Punjab with straight lasts and upturned toes, worked in silk, gold and silver thread (tilla): tilla jutti, Patiala jutti, mojari, khussa.
leaves.aliases: Punjabi jutti; mojari; khussa; tilla jutti
leaves.see: H4-82 Tatar Leather Mosaic. Possession taxonomy: Jutti (A2 Footwear); Mojari (A2 Footwear); Khussa (A2 Footwear).

leaves.label: Western Leatherwork
leaves.defn: the tooled, carved and silver-mounted leather of the vaquero and cowboy tradition, from Iberia and New Spain to the American West, Hawaii and the Great Basin: vaquero saddles, Sheridan-style floral carving, buckaroo gear, cowboy boots.
leaves.aliases: vaquero saddlery; Western saddlery; Western leather carving

leaves.defn: vegetable-tanned leather of Fez and Marrakech cut, stitched and embroidered in silk and metal thread on poufs, slippers and bags: embroidered poufs, babouches.
